youtube_title: Hospital Says 'Police Case First'? The Supreme Court Says Treat First #Shorts
youtube_description:
Rules You Didn't Know #6. After an accident, a hospital can't say 'police case first, treatment later'. In Pt. Parmanand Katara v. Union of India (1989), the Supreme Court held that every doctor, whether at a government hospital or otherwise, has a duty to give immediate medical aid to save a life, and police or procedural formalities can't delay it. And the person who brings the injured in is a Good Samaritan, protected by law: they can't be forced to give their name or pay. In an emergency, call 112 or 108 and take them to the nearest hospital.
Source: Supreme Court, Parmanand Katara v. Union of India (1989); Good Samaritan protection (SC guidelines 2016, Motor Vehicles Act s.134A).
